archetype_reasoning: This practice is built around radical accessibility — walk-ins, evenings, weekends, sliding scale, fearful patients welcome. That's pure Helper: calming, clarity-first, patient-centered. But they're also a Challenger in the SA dental market, because they break every convention (no appointment needed, open when others close, spa-level comfort at budget prices). The design must feel warm enough to reduce anxiety AND confident enough to signal that 6 years of 'America's Best Dentist' is earned. Competitors default to clinical white — we diverge with warmth. This is the neighborhood hero who also happens to be the most decorated dentist in the city.

design_direction.name: Warm South Texas Authority
design_direction.metaphor: A beautifully maintained neighborhood clinic that's quietly been winning national awards for six years — unpretentious on the outside, exceptional on the inside. Like walking into a trusted neighbor's living room and discovering they're a world-class surgeon.
design_direction.rationale: The teal (#237D82) from the existing site is the one brand asset worth inheriting — it signals healthcare trust and calm. We evolve it rather than abandon it. Warm cream replaces the clinical gray background, immediately signaling welcome over sterility. Amber becomes the CTA and emergency accent, referencing San Antonio's golden hour light and creating urgency without alarm. DM Serif Display for headings gives Dr. Humphrey's credentials the gravitas they've earned, while Plus Jakarta Sans body copy stays warm and approachable for anxious patients scanning for reassurance.

background.name: Warm Cream
background.role: Page background — warm off-white replacing the dated #EEEEEE gray. Signals welcome, not sterility.

surface.name: Clean White
surface.role: Cards, panels, modals — pure white for maximum contrast against warm cream sections

foreground.name: Deep Tide
foreground.role: Primary text — teal-inflected near-black; connects visually to brand teal while maintaining WCAG AA contrast (>16:1 on cream)

muted.name: Coastal Slate
muted.role: Secondary text, borders, dividers, placeholder text

brand_primary.name: Reef Teal
brand_primary.role: Signature brand color — evolved from existing #237D82 (slightly more vivid and confident). Used for section backgrounds, nav, headings, icons. The through-line of brand identity.

brand_accent.name: Golden Hour
brand_accent.role: CTAs, emergency/walk-in callouts, award badges, interactive highlights. Warm amber — references San Antonio's golden light, creates urgency without alarm. Contrasts beautifully against both teal and cream.

display_font.name: DM Serif Display
display_font.weight: 400 (regular — the font is inherently bold at display sizes)
display_font.feeling: Elegant authority with warmth — not stiff corporate serif, not informal script. At 72px it commands respect. At 48px it feels like a trusted voice. Perfect vehicle for 'America's Best Dentist' without feeling cold or academic.

body_font.name: Plus Jakarta Sans
body_font.feeling: Warm, modern, human. Rounded terminals prevent the clinical sharpness of Inter or Roboto. Highly readable at 16–18px. Pairs with DM Serif via contrast: serif gravitas headlines, humanist sans warmth in body.

accent_font.name: DM Mono
accent_font.use_case: Award year callouts ('2021 · 2022 · 2023 · 2024 · 2025 · 2026'), stat numbers ('15+ 5-star reviews'), hours display, badge text. Monospaced precision reads as clinical rigor — perfect contrast for the credential and award content.

layout.navigation: Sticky header — transparent on scroll-top over hero, solid Reef Teal on scroll. Left: logo. Center: nav links (Home, Services, About, Testimonials, Contact). Right: 'Book Your Visit' amber pill button + phone number.
layout.card_style: rounded-xl (16px radius), white fill, subtle shadow (0 2px 16px rgba(26,43,44,0.08)), no border — floating card feel signals modern and premium
layout.button_style: Pill-shaped (999px radius) — friendly and approachable, not clinical. Primary: Golden Hour amber fill, Deep Tide text. Secondary: Reef Teal outline, Reef Teal text. Ghost: transparent, white text for dark sections.
layout.dividers: None — section color blocks handle separation. No horizontal rules or wave SVGs.
layout.image_treatment: Hero: full-bleed photo with Deep Tide overlay (60% opacity) to ensure text legibility. Content sections: constrained (max 600px wide), rounded-2xl (24px radius), subtle shadow. Team: circular crop for portraits.
layout.section_padding: 120px vertical on desktop, 80px on tablet, 60px on mobile

tone_and_copy.headline_style: Transformation-first: lead with the patient outcome or relief, not the service. 'Tooth Emergency? We're Open Right Now' beats 'Emergency Dental Services Available'.
tone_and_copy.cta_language: Action + time: 'Book Your Visit', 'Walk In Today', 'Call Now', 'We'll See You Today'. Avoid: 'Learn More', 'Get Started', 'Submit'.
avoid: Clinical stock photography (blue-gloved hands, extracted teeth, isolated equipment)
Jargon without translation (write 'Root Canal' then immediately add 'Pain relief, usually 1 visit')
Corporate voice — this practice is a neighborhood hero, not a hospital chain
Fear-based copy ('Don't ignore tooth pain — it gets worse') — this audience is already anxious
Generic dental clichés ('Your smile is our priority', 'We care about your health')

always: Lead every section with a patient outcome or relief — not a feature or service name
Show Dr. Humphrey's awards prominently — 6 consecutive years is extraordinary social proof that the current site buries
Golden Hour amber is reserved exclusively for emergency/walk-in CTAs and the trust bar — don't dilute it
Every CTA must include the phone number as a secondary option — South SA audience converts heavily by phone
Maintain generous whitespace — the practice's warmth should breathe through the layout
Use DM Mono for any number, year, or stat — it adds precision and credibility
Images must show people (patients, staff) — not equipment or teeth closeups
never: Never use the original #EEEEEE gray background — it reads dated and cold
Never bury awards or credentials in body copy paragraphs — they are visual design assets, use them as such
Never use more than 2 fonts on any single page (DM Serif Display + Plus Jakarta Sans; DM Mono for accent only)
Never use clinical stock photography — it contradicts the comfort positioning
Never show more than 3 primary navigation items on mobile — hamburger menu for full nav
Never use Reef Teal and Golden Hour adjacent to each other at full saturation — always separate with white or cream
Never leave the contact form without confirmation state — broken forms destroyed trust on the current site

brief_summary: Complete visual overhaul for 6 to 9 Dental — a Helper/Challenger archetype practice that is South San Antonio's most awarded dental office hiding behind a 2016 Wix template. Direction: 'Warm South Texas Authority'. Palette: Reef Teal (#1A7F86) + Golden Hour amber (#E8924A) on Warm Cream (#FEFBF5). Fonts: DM Serif Display (authority headings) + Plus Jakarta Sans (warm body) + DM Mono (awards/stats). 10-section homepage leads with a full-bleed hero proclaiming their award record, immediately followed by a trust bar of all 6 consecutive Best Dentist years. Section flow: hero → awards → 3 accessibility reasons → comfort promise → services → Dr. Humphrey spotlight → testimonials → emergency CTA → location. Primary CTA is always the phone number or walk-in call — this audience converts by phone. The new site should make a dental-anxious, budget-conscious South SA working parent feel seen and safe within 5 seconds.
